extracted.intended_audience: applicants, representatives, patent attorneys, and industrial property offices in ARIPO Contracting States (users of the Harare Protocol)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for filing, examining, granting, maintaining and enforcing ARIPO patents, utility models and industrial designs under the Harare Protocol (including procedural requirements, substantive patentability criteria, fees, appeals and administrative rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patents shall be granted for any inventions in all fields of technology, provided that they are new, involve an inventive step and are susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8(1). These three elements (novelty, inventive step/non-obviousness, industrial applicability) are the core substantive criteria for grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (not inventions as such)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following, in particular, shall not be regarded as inventions: (a) discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; (b) aesthetic creations; (c) schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts, playing games or doing business, and programs for computers; and (d) presentations of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 8(2)-(3). Exclusion applies only to the extent the application or patent relates to such subject matter 'as such.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to patentability (public order/morality and excluded categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO patents shall not be granted in respect of inventions of which commercial exploitation would be contrary to public order or morality; plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals; and methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 9(1). Paragraphs 9(2) and 9(3) clarify that microbiological processes and their products are not excluded and that products for use in excluded methods may still be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / prior art definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered to be new if it is not anticipated by prior art. Prior art means everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by means of a written disclosure, including drawings and other illustrations, or an oral disclosure, by use or by display at an exhibition, provided that such publication occurred before the date of filing of the ARIPO patent application or, where priority is claimed, before the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 10(1)-(2). Also includes earlier-filed ARIPO applications published after the date (Section 10(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier ARIPO applications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of ARIPO patent applications filed prior to the relevant date and published on or after that date shall be considered as comprised in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 10(3). Documents within the meaning of Section 10(3) are treated specially for inventive step (see Section 12(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosures (6-month grace periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the invention shall not be taken into consideration for novelty if it occurred not more than six (6) months before the filing date and if it was due to or in consequence of an evident abuse in relation to the applicant or the applicant displayed the invention at an official or officially recognised international exhibition (with supporting certificate) within that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11(1)-(2). Applicant must file a supporting certificate within the time limit prescribed in the Regulations when relying on exhibition disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step / non-obviousness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the State of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 12(1). Documents deemed prior art under Section 10(3) shall not be considered in deciding inventive step (Section 12(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered susceptible of industrial applicability if it can be made or utilized in any kind of industry, including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 13. This is the standard for 'utility' of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to file and right to a patent (ownership rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to an ARIPO patent shall belong to the inventor or his successor in title; where the inventor is an employee, rights are determined in accordance with the law of the Contracting State; where two or more persons made an invention independently, the right belongs to the person whose application has the earliest filing date or priority date (if published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 16(1)-(3). Also Section 14 permitting persons possessing the right to file an ARIPO patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO patent application by non-entitled persons (court-determined rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person other than the applicant who has been adjudged by a final decision of a court of a Designated State to be entitled to the grant may prosecute the application in place of the applicant, file a new application, or request refusal, in accordance with the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 17(1)-(2). Remedies and procedures are governed by the Regulations and Section 28 mutatis mutandis for new filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of the inventor to be mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor shall have the right to be mentioned as such in an ARIPO patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 18. Recognition of inventorship is guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative requirement for non-resident applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who does not reside or have principal place of business in a Contracting State shall appoint a representative to act in all proceedings established by the Protocol and Regulations; applicants resident in a Contracting State may be represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 19. Representative must be legally recognized and authorisation through power of attorney is contemplated (see definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for ARIPO patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of an ARIPO patent shall be 20 years from the date of filing of the application, subject to the payment of maintenance fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 20. Maintenance fee payment is a condition to maintain the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and lapse for non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or holder shall pay the annual maintenance fees as prescribed in the Regulations; where the annual maintenance fee is not paid as prescribed, the application or patent shall lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 4(1)-(2), 21(1)-(2). Regulations prescribe amounts and payment manner; failure to pay causes lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by an ARIPO patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent shall confer on its proprietor the same rights as would be conferred by a national patent granted in that Designated State; alleged infringements shall be enforced in accordance with the national law of the State in which the alleged infringement occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 22(1)-(2). Effect and enforcement are subject to national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection by publication of an ARIPO patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall, on the date of its publication, provisionally confer upon the applicant the protection provided for in Section 22 in the Designated States unless the national law of the Designated State provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 23. Publication-based provisional rights may vary depending on national provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of protection determined by claims and interpreted by description/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the protection conferred by an ARIPO patent or application shall be determined by the terms of the claims; the description and drawings shall be used to interpret the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 24. Claims are primary; description/drawings are interpretative aids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and licensing of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of an ARIPO patent application or an ARIPO patent may be transferred with respect to one or more Designated States; recordal must be requested in writing and signed by the parties; an application or patent may be licensed in whole or in part for whole or part of territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 25. Recordal and fees are prescribed in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable national law for granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted by the Office shall, in each Designated State, be subject to provisions of the applicable national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 26. National law governs many aspects of effect, enforcement, and certain substantive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and transmission (where to file)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be filed with the Office or, where national law permits, with the industrial property office of that Contracting State; an application filed with a national office has the same effect as filing at the Office; national laws governing inventions not communicable abroad or requiring initial national filing are respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 27(1)-(3). If filed at a national office it must be transmitted to ARIPO as prescribed in the Regulations (Section 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO divisional application shall be filed directly with the Office and only in respect of subject matter which does not extend beyond the scope of an earlier application as filed; it is deemed filed on the earlier filing date and enjoys the same priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 28(1)-(2). Designated States in the earlier application are deemed designated in the divisional unless applicant communicates otherwise (Section 28(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation rules and permitted filing languages
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be filed in any language; an application filed in a language other than English shall be translated into English within the period prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 30(1)-(2). Timely translation is required to proceed in the ARIPO system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an ARIPO patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall contain: (a) a request for the grant of an ARIPO patent; (b) a description of the invention; (c) one or more claims; (d) drawings where necessary; and (e) an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 31(1). Applications must satisfy additional requirements in the Regulations and payment of prescribed fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States and associated fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of an ARIPO patent shall be requested for one or more of the Contracting States; designation is subject to payment of a designation fee; designations may be withdrawn or added (subject to prescribed fees and timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 32(1)-(4). Adding may be possible before publication under Section 43(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an ARIPO patent application shall be the date on which the filing requirements, as provided under Section 31(1)(a) to (c) (request, description, one or more claims), are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 33. Meeting minimum requirements is essential to secure filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked that they form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 34. Unity is a formal requirement and affects divisionaling and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must enable the skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: A description shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art; disclosure must be entirely effected by an enabling description with accompanying drawings, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 35(1)-(2). This is the written description / enablement requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims clarity and support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim or claims shall, in a clear and concise manner, define the matter for which protection is sought and shall be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 36. Claims must be consistent with the description and not ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract role limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract shall merely serve as a source of technical information and shall not be used for the purposes of interpreting the scope of the protection sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 37. Abstract is informational only, not interpretative for claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right (12-month rule) and equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has duly applied for a patent to a Paris Convention State or WTO member shall enjoy, for filing for an ARIPO patent application, a right of priority during a period of 12 months from the date of filing the first application; filings equivalent to regular national filings under national law or under bilateral/multilateral agreements are recognized as giving rise to priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 38(1)-(3). Priority effects are governed by Sections 39-40 for claiming and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority (declaration and documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant intending to take advantage of priority must file a declaration of priority and any other document required in accordance with the Regulations; multiple priorities may be claimed and may apply to a single claim; the right of priority covers only elements included in the earlier application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 39(1)-(5). Time limits running from priority run from the earliest priority date when multiple priorities are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of priority right on prior art date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of priority shall count as the date of filing of the ARIPO patent application for the purposes of novelty and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 40. Priority date replaces filing date for determining prior art in Sections 10(2)-(3) and Section 16(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on filing and filing-date notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine whether filing requirements have been complied with; where complied with the Office shall accord the filing date and notify the applicant and each Designated State; where not complied with, the Office shall invite compliance within the period prescribed and may refuse if not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 41(1)-(5). Filing date confers equivalence to national filing in Designated States (Section 41(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements examination and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall examine whether the formal requirements prescribed in the Regulations have been complied with; it shall notify compliance or invite correction; non-compliance within the period results in deemed withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 42(1)-(4). Formal compliance separate from substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall publish the ARIPO patent application as soon as possible after expiry of 18 months from filing (or priority), or earlier at the applicant's request subject to payment of fee; if decision to grant is effective before 18 months, publication occurs at the same time as the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 43(1)-(2). Publication triggers third-party observations and provisional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations by third parties after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Following publication, any person may present observations concerning the patentability of the invention as prescribed in the Regulations; the third party shall not be a party to the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 44(1)-(2). Third party submissions are allowed but do not make them parties to prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination on request and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall, on request and upon payment of prescribed fees, undertake or arrange for the search and substantive examination to determine whether requirements of the Protocol are met; the request is not deemed filed until fees paid; failure to request within specified period causes lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 45(1)-(5). Examination invites office action and opportunity to amend; failure to respond can lead to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant and communications from Designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office decides to grant it shall notify the applicant and each Designated State; each Designated State may within prescribed period make written communication whether the patent shall have effect in its territory or have no effect for specified reasons; applicant may request reconsideration and submit amendments/arguments; failure of Designated State to respond may be deemed refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 46(1)-(4). Designated State procedures may lead to per-state effect of the ARIPO grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during prosecution (no added matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be amended in proceedings before the Office in accordance with the Regulations; the applicant may amend description, claims or drawings subject to fee; an application may not be amended to contain subject matter extending beyond the content of the initial application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 47(1)-(3). Amendments are allowed but cannot introduce new matter (added matter prohibition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant or refusal and remedies (appeal or national processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office is satisfied, it shall grant an ARIPO patent (effective in Designated States that did not object); where it does not fulfill requirements, the Office shall refuse and notify applicant, who may lodge an appeal to the Board of Appeal or request treatment in any Designated State as a national application; failure to file required further requests leads to lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 48(1)-(7). Conversion to national processing and appeals are remedial options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of granted ARIPO patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall publish the ARIPO patent granted as provided for in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 49. Publication procedures and timing are in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant limitation / amendment of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent may be limited by post-grant amendment at the request of the proprietor; request filed per Regulations and fee; any amendment to claims shall fall wholly within the scope of the claims before the amendment; re-examination and re-publication occur subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 50(1)-(3). Post-grant amendments cannot broaden claim scope beyond original claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO Patent Register maintenance and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall maintain an ARIPO Patent Register containing particulars specified in the Regulations; no entry shall be made before publication; register open to public inspection subject to prescribed fees and confidentiality rules for unpublished applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 51-52. Inspection restrictions apply to unpublished files and withdrawn applications; courts/authorities access via copies or extracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to national patent application after ARIPO refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office refuses an application, the industrial property office of a Designated State shall, at the request of the applicant, apply the procedure for the grant of a national patent; request submitted to Office per Regulations and transmission to national offices occurs upon payment of conversion fee; effect of ARIPO filing lapses if conversion not timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 53(1)-(5). Conversion enables national prosecution when ARIPO grant fails in some Designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of patent application to utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before the grant or refusal, the applicant may convert the patent application into an application for a utility model upon request and payment of fees; conversion accords the filing date of the initial patent application; conversion is irrevocable and documents filed are deemed filed at conversion time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 54(1)-(4). Useful option to pursue utility model protection instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of rights for missed time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or proprietor who was unable to observe a time limit in spite of all due care required by the circumstances may have rights restored upon request if requirements in the Regulations are met; restoration may be refused for certain time limits and has retroactive legal consequences when granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 55(1)-(6). Regulations set requirements and limits; good-faith users in the interim may continue use without payment in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international applications and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating a Contracting State bound by the PCT shall be considered to be an application under this Protocol; the Patent Cooperation Treaty applies in addition and prevails in case of conflict; annual fees under Section 21 are deferred until applicable PCT time limits expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 56(1)-(3) and Sections 57-58 regarding ARIPO acting as receiving, designated or elected Office under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model protection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO utility models shall be registered for inventions in all fields of technology provided they are new and susceptible of industrial application; certain patent provisions apply mutatis mutandis; no utility model where claimed subject matter already the subject of a patent or utility model registration based on a prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 59-61. Utility models have different substantive thresholds (inventive step may be omitted) and specific applicability is described in Section 60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection of an ARIPO utility model shall be 10 years from the filing date, subject to payment of maintenance fees; national shorter/longer terms apply in respective Designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 62(1)-(2). Transitional rules for earlier registrations may apply (Section 62(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination and conversion rules for utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall undertake or arrange for search and substantive examination of utility model applications in accordance with the Regulations; sections on examination and failure to respond apply mutatis mutandis; an applicant may convert a utility model application to a patent application before refusal or registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 63-64. Conversion accorded initial filing date; conversion only once under Section 64(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design protection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO industrial design shall have effect and be subject to same conditions as a national industrial design; novelty is assessed according to the provisions of the national laws of the Designated State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 65-67. Many patent provisions apply mutatis mutandis to industrial designs (Section 66 lists applicable sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of an ARIPO industrial design
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of the ARIPO industrial design registration shall be 15 years from the filing date subject to payment of maintenance fees; national shorter/longer terms apply in respective Designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 68(1)-(2). Transitional provisions for earlier registrations may apply (Section 68(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO industrial design application shall contain: (a) a request for registration; (b) a reproduction of the industrial design; and (c) a Statement of novelty; the application must satisfy requirements in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 69(1)-(2). Fees apply mutatis mutandis to Section 31(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and substantive examination of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall publish an industrial design application on filing and on registration; where the application complies with formal requirements it shall be transmitted to each Designated State for substantive examination in accordance with national law and each Designated State may communicate whether registration will have effect in its territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 70 and 72(1)-(2). Designated State communications and applicant reconsideration procedures apply mutatis mutandis (Section 72(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration or refusal of industrial design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office is satisfied that the requirements have been fulfilled, it shall register an ARIPO industrial design, which will have effect in Designated States that did not object; early registration at applicant's request may be possible where all Designated States agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 73(1)-(3). Refusal and appeals procedures apply mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Appeal composition and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board of Appeal shall consist of five members experienced in IP matters (two of whom shall be patent examiners); three members form a quorum and at least one patent examiner must be present; members appointed for two-year renewable terms; functions include considering appeals against Office decisions, reviewing final decisions, and deciding matters incidental to its powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 74(1)-(7). The Administrative Council adopts the Board's Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to appeal and effect of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A party adversely affected by any final decision of the Office may appeal; an appeal shall operate as a stay of all subsequent actions on the application until the Board determines the appeal; notice of appeal must be filed within the period prescribed and not deemed filed until appeal fees are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 75-77. Board decision is final (Section 78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations-making power and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council shall make Regulations for the implementation of the Protocol and may amend them; the Regulations shall relate in particular to administrative requirements, matters of procedure, details necessary for implementation and the fees to be charged and distribution of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 79(1)-(2). Regulations provide the detailed procedural, fee and timing rules underpinning the Protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and distribution of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may levy fees for any official task or procedure under the Protocol; amounts of fees and the manner of payment shall be prescribed in the Regulations; fees collected shall be distributed between the Office and the Contracting States as prescribed in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 4(1)-(3) and 5. Failure to pay fees in due time causes lapse of application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits, computation and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Protocol does not specify a time limit, such time limits shall be prescribed in the Regulations; Regulations shall specify time limits to be observed, the manner of computation and conditions under which time limits may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(1)-(2). Regulations control all procedural deadlines and extension conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force, accession, denunciation and amendment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: States may become parties by signature and ratification or accession; the Protocol enters into force following deposit of required instruments as prescribed; a Contracting State may denounce the Protocol with 6-month effect; amendments may be proposed and adopted by two-thirds of Contracting States with dates of entry into force determined by Council of Ministers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 80, 81 and 83. These procedural rules govern treaty status, withdrawal and amendment.
